cards.title: Countable and uncountable
cards.body: Countable nouns: you can count them — **one apple, two apples**. Uncountable nouns: you cannot count them one by one — **water, advice** — and they have no plural. The test: can you say **one ___**? *one chair* ✓ countable · *one water* ✗ uncountable. Careful: Czech counts some of these — *jedna rada* — but English does not: *an advice* ✗ · **some advice** ✓. The test cannot find these words; they must be learned (the **Countable in Czech** card has the list).
cards.body_cz: Počitatelná = 1, 2, 3… (jablko, jablka). Nepočitatelná = nedají se počítat po jednom (voda, rada) — bez množného čísla. Pozor: rada je česky počitatelná, advice anglicky ne.

cards.title: Common uncountables
points: Use some / a lot of / much
cards.body: These English nouns are uncountable (no a/an, no plural -s in the usual sense).
cards.body_cz: V angličtině nepočitatelná — ne a/an, ne běžné množné -s.

cards.title: a / an / some / any
points: some/any with plural countable or uncountable

cards.title: How many / How much
points: How many → countable · How much → uncountable

cards.title: Countable in Czech — not in English
points: Use some / a lot of / a piece of advice

cards.title: Practice focus
points: some/any with plural countable or uncountable

cards.title: Remember
points: uncountable: some · much · little · no a/an
